rituals.title: THE FIRST FRAME
rituals.goal: Catch the thought before it becomes the room.
rituals.steps:
1. Trigger — A trigger flickers.
2. Pause Story — Do not explain it yet.
3. Capture Thought — Pin the first thought, picture, or prediction exactly as it arrived.
4. Quote — Put quotation marks around it.
5. Close Capture — The catch ends there; no life story, no courtroom, no spiral.
rituals.win: ✓ One thought stayed one thought; the courtroom never opened.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Close Capture”; loosen the label.
• Pulled back? Touch “Capture Thought”.
• “Quote” — the rule loosened.
• “Trigger” versus “Close Capture”: what eased?
• I can use “Pause Story” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Trigger → Pause Story → Capture Thought → Quote → Close Capture
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if holding the thought in mind makes you feel less steady or more upset.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
rituals.goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Trays — Imagine two trays.
2. Name Sides — Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
3. Sort Facts — Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
4. Switch Sides — Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
5. Balance Verdict — Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.
rituals.win: ✓ Both trays stayed visible; the verdict stopped being one-sided.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Balance Verdict”; let feeling settle.
• Use “Sort Facts” on return.
• “Switch Sides” separates feeling from fact.
• “Imagine Trays” → “Balance Verdict”: what changed?
• I can use “Name Sides” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Trays → Name Sides → Sort Facts → Switch Sides → Balance Verdict
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Quit when you are recycling arguments instead of discovering evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
rituals.goal: A worst-case story loses size when it gains a route.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Fear — Picture the feared ending in one line.
2. Build Exits — Under it build four rungs: WHAT HAPPENS; WHAT I DO NEXT; WHO OR WHAT HELPS; HOW RECOVERY COULD BEGIN.
3. Add Likely — Add a fifth rung for the outcome that is actually most likely.
4. Climb Route — Move through the five steps once in your mind.
5. Act Now — Then take the first coping action available now.
rituals.win: ✓ The forecast lost its monopoly.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Act Now”; leave the forecast.
• Shortcut: “Add Likely”, once.
• “Climb Route” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Name Fear” → “Act Now”?
• I can use “Build Exits” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Fear → Build Exits → Add Likely → Climb Route → Act Now
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not run this alone for immediate danger, medical crisis, or trauma flooding.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE GREY DIAL
rituals.goal: Binary thinking hates a numbered dial.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Extremes — Name the two extremes your mind is using.
2. Build Scale — Build a 0–10 scale between them and say three real anchor points: 2, 5, and 8.
3. Place Today — Place today’s event where the evidence fits—not where the emotion shouts.
4. Choose Response — Choose a response matched to that exact setting.
rituals.win: ✓ The dial found a middle, and the response found its size.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Response”; keep both sides.
• Restart detected: “Place Today”.
• “Place Today” widens the evidence field.
• “Name Extremes” versus “Choose Response”: what eased?
• I can use “Build Scale” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Extremes → Build Scale → Place Today → Choose Response
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if grading becomes another perfection test.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BORROW THEIR MIRROR
rituals.goal: Use the standard you reserve for someone you respect.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Trusted — Imagine a trusted person bringing you the same facts.
2. Offer Allowances — Hold the questions you would ask them, the allowances you would make, and the evidence you would require before judging them.
3. Remove Name — Now remove their name.
4. Apply Page — Apply that page to yourself without adding a harsher clause.
rituals.win: ✓ The label lost some of its legal power.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Apply Page”; loosen the label.
• Re-entry move: “Remove Name”.
• “Remove Name” — the rule loosened.
• What changed: “Imagine Trusted” → “Apply Page”?
• I can use “Offer Allowances” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Trusted → Offer Allowances → Remove Name → Apply Page
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Leave the mirror if it excuses harm or becomes forced positivity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE RULE UNDER THE RULE
rituals.goal: A surface thought often works for a hidden constitution.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Painful — Picture the painful thought.
2. Ask Meaning — Ask, ‘If that were true, what would it mean about me, others, or life?’ Answer quickly, then ask the same question of the answer.
3. Continue Stable — Continue only until one stable rule repeats.
4. Box Rule — Put that rule in a mental box.
5. Apply Today — Today’s task is to inspect it, not obey it.
rituals.win: ✓ I inspected the hidden rule without obeying it.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Apply Today”; release the score.
• Loop back? Use “Continue Stable”.
• “Box Rule” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Picture Painful” → “Apply Today”?
• I can use “Ask Meaning” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Painful → Ask Meaning → Continue Stable → Box Rule → Apply Today
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop descent if it triggers feeling unreal or disconnected, hopelessness, or overwhelming material.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE SCHEMA CONTRABAND FILE
rituals.goal: Smuggle what does not fit reality past the old filter.
rituals.steps:
1. Capture — Catch one event your negative self-story would normally delete.
2. Describe Happened — Say what happened, why it really does not fit the old rule, and which convenient excuse the rule will use to dismiss it.
3. Sign — Sign the entry as usable evidence and reread it tomorrow once—no chanting.
rituals.win: ✓ The story became one version instead of the constitution.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Sign”; loosen the label.
• Catch restart with “Describe Happened”.
• “Describe Happened” — the rule loosened.
• Difference check: “Capture” → “Sign”.
• I can use “Describe Happened” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Capture → Describe Happened → Sign
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use exceptions to deny real problems that need action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE FORECAST SCOREBOARD
rituals.goal: Memory edits its predictions after the result.
rituals.steps:
1. Count Hit — Before an uncertain event, remember four items: prediction, confidence %, deadline, and what counts as a hit.
2. Keep Result — Afterward, hold the result without rewriting the original entry.
3. Calculate — Calculate the gap between confidence and reality.
4. Spot the Bias — After five rounds, look for your recurring bias.
rituals.win: ✓ Forecast bias exposed. Memory cannot quietly rewrite the scoreboard now.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Spot the Bias”; release the score.
• Return once to “Calculate”.
• “Calculate” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Count Hit” → “Spot the Bias”?
• I can use “Keep Result” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Count Hit → Keep Result → Calculate → Spot the Bias
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Retire the ledger if it feeds compulsive monitoring.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE SKY DOES NOT BECOME THE WEATHER
rituals.goal: Content changes; the capacity to notice keeps showing up.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Thought — Name one thought, one feeling, and one role active now.
2. Say Being — For each, say: ‘This is being noticed.’ Search for the noticing itself—its colour, age, or mood.
3. Rest Openness — If none can be found, rest with that openness for ten seconds.
4. Land in Feet — Return by feeling both feet.
rituals.win: ✓ Weather moved; the sky stayed. Both feet found the room again.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Land in Feet”; keep the compass.
• Shortcut: “Rest Openness”, once.
• “Rest Openness” keeps meaning in motion.
• Difference check: “Name Thought” → “Land in Feet”.
• I can use “Say Being” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Thought → Say Being → Rest Openness → Land in Feet
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid prolonged self-inquiry if it intensifies feeling unreal or detached from yourself or unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TRANSLATE THE VERDICT
rituals.goal: ‘Bad’ is compressed data. Decompress it.
rituals.steps:
1. Take Judgement — Take one judgement and mentally translate it into three components: visible facts, personal preference, likely consequence.
2. Prefer Decision — Example: ‘Awful meeting’ becomes ‘Two interruptions; I prefer turn-taking; the decision stayed unclear.’ Respond to the components rather than fighting the label.
rituals.win: ✓ I unpacked the verdict into facts I could actually respond to.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Prefer Decision”; leave the forecast.
• Pulled back? Touch “Prefer Decision”.
• “Take Judgement” — fear isn’t fate.
• Difference check: “Take Judgement” → “Prefer Decision”.
• I can use “Prefer Decision” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Take Judgement → Prefer Decision
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep moral language where clear ethical wrongdoing must be named.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE CRISIS MENU
rituals.goal: Choose before distress turns choice into fog.
rituals.steps:
1. Prepare Five — Prepare five ten-minute diversions across different channels: hands, movement, sound, practical task, safe contact.
2. Select Option — During a spike, select the first available option without browsing for the perfect one.
3. Finish Interval — Finish the interval, reassess safety, then either return or choose support.
rituals.win: ✓ Distress no longer has to invent the menu while it is hungry.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Interval”; release the score.
• On return: “Select Option”.
• “Select Option” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Look back: “Prepare Five” → “Finish Interval”.
• I can use “Select Option” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Prepare Five → Select Option → Finish Interval
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Diversion is not enough for suicidal intent, violence risk, overdose, or medical emergency.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: UPGRADE THE WAITING ROOM
rituals.goal: An unavoidable minute can still change quality.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick Best — Pick one lever for this interval: picture a supportive scene, connect the moment to meaning, offer a brief prayer, relax one area, or do one thing fully.
2. Use Lever — Use only one lever until the interval ends.
3. Upgrade the Minute — You are improving the room, not denying why you are there.
rituals.win: ✓ I upgraded the waiting minute without pretending I wanted to be there.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Upgrade the Minute”; no breath-holding.
• Re-entry move: “Use Lever”.
• “Use Lever” — alarm isn’t command.
• Before/after: “Pick Best” → “Upgrade the Minute”.
• I can use “Use Lever” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Pick Best → Use Lever → Upgrade the Minute
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Move from coping to problem-solving when the situation requires direct action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: DOES THE FEELING FIT THE FILE?
rituals.goal: Emotion deserves respect; facts determine the dose.
rituals.steps:
1. Separate Cards — Separate four cards: prompting event, meaning, verified evidence, actual present threat.
2. Compare Emotion — Compare the emotion’s intensity and duration with the fourth card.
3. Use Feeling — If they fit, use the feeling’s message.
4. Update Meaning — If they exceed it, regulate first and update the meaning.
rituals.win: ✓ Feeling respected; dosage handed back to the facts.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Update Meaning”; let feeling settle.
• Catch restart with “Use Feeling”.
• “Use Feeling” separates feeling from fact.
• Before/after: “Separate Cards” → “Update Meaning”.
• I can use “Compare Emotion” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Separate Cards → Compare Emotion → Use Feeling → Update Meaning
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Trust immediate protective action when evidence shows real threat.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: REVERSE THE URGE, COMPLETELY
rituals.goal: When the emotion is unjustified, half-opposites do not retrain it.
rituals.steps:
1. Check Support — Verify that the facts do not support the action impulse.
2. Speak Gently — Then do its full safe opposite: approach instead of avoid, speak gently instead of attack, straighten instead of collapse, engage instead of hide.
3. Match Posture — Match posture, words, and behaviour until the new signal is coherent.
rituals.win: ✓ Desire got a seat, not the steering wheel.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Match Posture”; let wanting crest.
• Re-entry move: “Speak Gently”.
• “Speak Gently” keeps wanting off controls.
• What lost power: “Check Support” → “Match Posture”?
• I can use “Speak Gently” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Check Support → Speak Gently → Match Posture
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Never oppose an urge that correctly protects you from danger or violation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: URGE IS NOT EMOTION
rituals.goal: Separate the weather from what it pushes you to do.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Emotion — Label the emotion in one word.
2. Hide Name — Name every behaviour it is urging—text, withdraw, shout, spend, hide, check.
3. Safe — Notice each SAFE, COSTLY, or UNCLEAR.
4. Choose Safe — Select a low-risk move that respects the emotion without automatically enacting its favourite instruction.
rituals.win: ✓ The feeling stayed as weather; the urge lost its marching orders.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Safe”; let wanting crest.
• Loop back? Use “Safe”.
• “Safe” keeps wanting off controls.
• Difference check: “Name Emotion” → “Choose Safe”.
• I can use “Hide Name” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Emotion → Hide Name → Safe → Choose Safe
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Get support if impulses involve harm, intoxication, or loss of control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LET THE EMOTION FINISH ONE CHAPTER
rituals.goal: Interrupted feelings keep restarting the book.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Chapter — Spot the current chapter only: sensation, meaning, action urge, or settling.
2. Permit — Permit the next natural chapter while withholding later ones.
3. Pause Meaning — If sensation is active, do not interpret; if meaning is clear, do not act yet.
4. Continue Genuine — Continue until a genuine settling marker—breath change, warmth, tears ending, posture release—appears.
rituals.win: ✓ One emotional chapter reached a real ending marker.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Continue Genuine”; let wanting crest.
• Restart detected: “Pause Meaning”.
• “Pause Meaning” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Continue Genuine”: what changed from “Identify Chapter”?
• I can use “Permit” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Chapter → Permit → Pause Meaning → Continue Genuine
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the process floods awareness or removes action control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: INSTALL THE CAPABLE MEMORY
rituals.goal: A resource becomes usable once it receives a body address.
rituals.steps:
1. Recall Real — Recall one real moment of courage, care, steadiness, or help.
2. Find Strongest — Find its strongest sensory detail and the body location that responds.
3. Add Small — Add a small gesture while the memory is vivid.
4. Release Gesture — Release, then use the gesture once to see whether the quality returns.
rituals.win: ✓ The capable state became easier to call back on purpose.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Release Gesture”; orient to now.
• On return: “Add Small”.
• “Add Small” moves memory toward then.
• Compare “Recall Real” with “Release Gesture”.
• I can use “Find Strongest” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Recall Real → Find Strongest → Add Small → Release Gesture
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Choose a different memory if the scene contains mixed threat or grief.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: STAMP WHERE THE DETAIL CAME FROM
rituals.goal: A memory matters without every detail carrying equal certainty.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick Detail — Choose one small memory detail; do not replay the event.
2. Tag Source — Stamp it SENSED, INFERRED, LEARNED LATER, or UNSURE.
3. Rate Confidence — Give the detail a confidence word—high, medium, low, or unknown—based on its source rather than its emotional intensity.
4. Keep Core — Picture one core fact that remains reliable and let the other detail keep its honest uncertainty.
rituals.win: ✓ The memory kept a reliable core and honest fog around the rest.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Core”; leave it unanswered.
• Skip replay; use “Rate Confidence”.
• “Rate Confidence” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• What changed: “Pick Detail” → “Keep Core”?
• I can use “Tag Source” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Pick Detail → Tag Source → Rate Confidence → Keep Core
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not force missing details; stop and seek support if the memory becomes overwhelming or disorienting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: OCEAN IN THE THROAT
rituals.goal: Use barely audible sound as a pace rail.
rituals.steps:
1. Create Soft — Narrow the throat only enough to create a soft ocean texture, never a rasp.
2. Let Sound — Let that sound accompany an easy inhale and exhale.
3. Reduce Effort — Reduce effort until someone beside you might barely hear it.
4. Release Technique — After several waves, release the technique completely.
rituals.win: ✓ Technique released. The calmer pace can stand on its own.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Release Technique”; then keep moving.
• Use “Reduce Effort” on return.
• “Reduce Effort” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Create Soft” → “Release Technique”.
• I can use “Let Sound” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Create Soft → Let Sound → Reduce Effort → Release Technique
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not practise through irritation, constriction, breathing illness, or dizziness.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: INSTALL THE COUNTER-QUALITY
rituals.goal: Do not wrestle a harmful tendency on its own ground.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Active — Name the active pattern and the wholesome quality opposite with it: cruelty/kindness, panic/steadiness, greed/sufficiency.
2. Act Counter — Produce one thought, posture, and act expressing the counter-quality.
3. Keep Credible — Keep it credible rather than grand.
4. Train — Train the opposite channel through embodiment.
rituals.win: ✓ The opposite quality got a real body, not just a good intention.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Train”; then keep moving.
• Pulled back? Touch “Keep Credible”.
• “Keep Credible” proves motion is available.
• “Name Active” versus “Train”: what eased?
• I can use “Act Counter” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Active → Act Counter → Keep Credible → Train
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Countering must not suppress valid grief, anger, or protective fear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ERASE THE OBJECT, KEEP THE CONTACT
rituals.goal: Let focus outlive its original target.
rituals.steps:
1. Stabilise — Stabilise attention on one simple form.
2. Remove Name — Gradually remove its name, meaning, shape, and boundary in that order.
3. Attend Object — Preserve the ongoing sense of attending as the object loses definition.
4. Rest Briefly — Rest briefly with contact that no longer depends on a clear thing.
rituals.win: ✓ The load became a sequence instead of a wall.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Rest Briefly”; release extra load.
• Loop back? Use “Attend Object”.
• “Attend Object” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “Stabilise” to “Rest Briefly”: what loosened?
• I can use “Remove Name” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Stabilise → Remove Name → Attend Object → Rest Briefly
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid object dissolution when prone to derealisation or perceptual instability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FIND THE FIRST ‘I’
rituals.goal: Sense of ‘I’ has an entrance point.
rituals.steps:
1. Experience — Notice an experience before describing it.
2. Wait Moment — Wait for the moment ‘I,’ ‘mine,’ or ‘about me’ attaches.
3. Trace Addition — Trace that addition to a body sensation, image, or location.
4. Observe Attachment — Observe the attachment without removing it.
5. Do the Task — The task is detection, not metaphysical victory.
rituals.win: ✓ I found the ‘I’ without needing to solve who ‘I’ ultimately am.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Do the Task”; no forcing.
• Return once to “Trace Addition”.
• “Observe Attachment” keeps sensation as data.
• Compare “Experience” with “Do the Task”.
• I can use “Wait Moment” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Experience → Wait Moment → Trace Addition → Observe Attachment → Do the Task
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the search produces feeling unreal or detached from yourself or panic.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE FIVE-LAYER INSPECTION
rituals.goal: Identity may be wearing several visible coats.
rituals.steps:
1. Move Body — Move through body, energy, mind, intellect, and deep ease.
2. Ask Change — At each layer ask what is present, what changes, and how it is known.
3. Keep All Layers — Do not discard any layer.
4. Place Like — Place them like translucent sheets within awareness, then select the layer needed for practical action.
rituals.win: ✓ Five layers became one usable next layer.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Place Like”; no forcing.
• Restart detected: “Keep All Layers”.
• “Keep All Layers” keeps sensation as data.
• What lost power: “Move Body” → “Place Like”?
• I can use “Ask Change” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Move Body → Ask Change → Keep All Layers → Place Like
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid abstract layer work when immediate grounding is needed.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE WAKING DREAM CHECK
rituals.goal: Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.
rituals.steps:
1. Take Event — Take one rigid reading of an event.
2. Compare Dream — Compare it with a dream: both organise fragments into a convincing world.
3. Identify Facts — Spot which facts are raw and which connections were constructed.
4. Try Construction — Try one alternate construction and observe how lived experience changes.
rituals.win: ✓ Another person’s response moved out of the judge’s chair.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Try Construction”; drop the scoreboard.
• Return once to “Identify Facts”.
• “Identify Facts” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• At “Try Construction”, compare “Take Event”.
• I can use “Compare Dream” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Take Event → Compare Dream → Identify Facts → Try Construction
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid dreamlike framing if it increases derealisation or psychotic symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RETURN THE PROJECTION TO SENDER
rituals.goal: The mind may be viewing its expectation on someone else’s screen.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Quality — Picture the quality you are assigning outward.
2. Ask Internal — Ask what internal expectation, fear, or rule would make that quality especially visible.
3. Name External — Name the external evidence separately.
4. Keep Facts — Keep what the facts support; return the excess meaning to your own inquiry.
rituals.win: ✓ Facts stayed; the extra projection went back for review.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Facts”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Name External”.
• “Name External” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Keep Facts”: what changed from “Picture Quality”?
• I can use “Ask Internal” without extra heat.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Quality → Ask Internal → Name External → Keep Facts
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Projection analysis must not erase another person’s documented behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CHANGE ONE LENS, WATCH THE WORLD
rituals.goal: Experience partly inherits the meaning that organises it.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Event — Choose a current event and picture the lens being used.
2. Replace Plausible — Replace it with one plausible alternative—not a positive slogan.
3. Act Lens — Spend five minutes acting from the alternate lens and observe changes in body, attention, and available choices.
rituals.win: ✓ I changed one lens and watched the available choices change with it.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Act Lens”; no breath-holding.
• Skip replay; use “Replace Plausible”.
• “Replace Plausible” — alarm isn’t command.
• Difference check: “Choose Event” → “Act Lens”.
• I can use “Replace Plausible” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Event → Replace Plausible → Act Lens
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Retain the original lens when evidence confirms danger or wrongdoing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BOX THE PROBLEM
rituals.goal: Scattered distress cannot be solved because it has no edges.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Lines — Picture three lines: CURRENT CONDITION; DESIRED CONDITION; MEASURABLE GAP.
2. Remove History — Remove history unless it changes the gap.
3. Give Problem — Give the problem a time horizon and one owner.
4. Statement — If the statement still contains ‘everything,’ shrink it again.
rituals.win: ✓ I boxed the problem until ‘everything’ could no longer fit inside it.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Statement”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Give Problem”.
• “Give Problem” keeps clarity above heat.
• Difference check: “Picture Lines” → “Statement”.
• I can use “Remove History” without extra heat.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Lines → Remove History → Give Problem → Statement
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Some pain needs witnessing rather than conversion into a problem.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FIXED, FLEXIBLE, UNKNOWN, ASSUMED
rituals.goal: Obstacles demand different tools depending on their category.
rituals.steps:
1. Name — Name every barrier.
2. Mark Category — Mark each barrier as fixed, flexible, unknown, or assumed.
3. Test Assumed — Accept the fixed, negotiate the flexible, investigate the unknown, and test the assumed.
4. Start What Moves — Begin with the highest-impact item whose category permits movement.
rituals.win: ✓ Care stayed; over-ownership did not.
rituals.supports:

• “Test Assumed” keeps responsibility proportionate.

rituals.formula_flow: Name → Mark Category → Test Assumed → Start What Moves
rituals.safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE NO-JUDGEMENT OPTION STORM
rituals.goal: Evaluation kills possibilities before they are born.
rituals.steps:
1. Start Brief — Start a brief timer and generate options without ranking, explaining, or defending them.
2. Include Conventional — Include one conventional, one tiny, one reversible, one collaborative, and one strange-but-safe possibility.
3. Test Feasibility — Only after the timer ends may feasibility enter the room.
rituals.win: ✓ I let options multiply before judgement was allowed into the room.

rituals.safety:

Exclude choices that violate ethics, consent, law, or safety from the start.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: DECIDE THE STOPPING LINE FIRST
rituals.goal: Analysis cannot finish if ‘enough’ has no definition.
rituals.steps:
1. State Minimum — Before researching, state the minimum evidence required to choose: number of quotes, critical facts, confidence level, or deadline.

3. Select Further — When the threshold is met, select; further information needs a new reason for entry.
rituals.win: ✓ Clarity survived the emotion.
rituals.supports:

• On return: “Picture Genuinely”.

rituals.title: THE AFTERSHOCK CLOCK
rituals.goal: Residual body alarm is not fresh evidence.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Reasonable — Set a reasonable after-event window during which shakiness, replay, fatigue, or emotion are expected echoes.
2. Picture Time — Picture its end time.
3. Notice Sensations — Until then, keep sensations but forbid them from changing your meaning of what happened.
4. Reassess — Reassess after recovery and sleep where possible.
rituals.win: ✓ I recognised the aftershock as residue, not fresh evidence.
rituals.supports:

• “Notice Sensations” proves motion is available.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME
rituals.goal: Analysis may keep interrupting an unfinished inner sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Bring Image — Bring up the image gently and prohibit verbal commentary.
2. Allow Move — Allow it to move at its own speed until it reaches a stable frame or natural ending.
3. Check Your Position — Notice whether your position, distance, or available action changes.
4. Use Sensory — Reorient afterward using present sensory facts.
rituals.win: ✓ I let the image reach its last frame instead of interrupting it with analysis.
rituals.supports:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
rituals.goal: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.
rituals.steps:
1. Keep Both Versions — The moment an outcome differs from expectation, keep both versions verbatim.
2. State Size — State the size and direction of the error.
3. Name Miss — Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy.
4. Preserve Forecast — Do not let hindsight rewrite the original prediction.
rituals.win: ✓ Original prediction preserved. Hindsight cannot edit the miss now.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Preserve Forecast”; slow the clock.
• Shortcut: “Name Miss”, once.
• “Name Miss” puts facts above speed.
• “Keep Both Versions” to “Preserve Forecast”: what loosened?
• I can use “State Size” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Keep Both Versions → State Size → Name Miss → Preserve Forecast

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CONFIDENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE
rituals.goal: Certainty and support need separate meters.
rituals.steps:
1. Rate Sure — Rate how sure you feel from 0–100.
2. Rate Evidence — Independently rate evidence quality using source reliability, directness, and recency.
3. Separate Meters — Picture the two scores on separate meters so certainty cannot masquerade as evidence.
4. Follow Evidence — Let the evidence meter choose the action; treat the confidence meter as a feeling to notice, not a vote.
rituals.win: ✓ Evidence got the vote. Confidence stayed a feeling.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Follow Evidence”; end the lap.
• On return: “Separate Meters”.
• “Separate Meters” proves loops can stop.

• I can use “Rate Evidence” without another lap.
rituals.formula_flow: Rate Sure → Rate Evidence → Separate Meters → Follow Evidence
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Urgent protective instincts may require action while evidence is gathered.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PUT AN EXPIRY DATE ON THE CONCLUSION
rituals.goal: Old evidence should not command new conditions forever.
rituals.steps:
1. Estimate Quickly — Estimate how quickly the conclusion’s evidence can become stale.
2. Give Renewal — Give it a renewal date plus the data required then.
3. Use Temporaryly — Until review, use it temporaryly; after expiry, it must be renewed by current evidence before influencing behaviour.
rituals.win: ✓ The story now has to coexist with what does not fit.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: SAME FACTS, THREE ASSUMPTIONS
rituals.goal: Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.
rituals.steps:
1. Keep Observations — Keep all observations fixed.
2. Reframe Three Ways — Run the same facts through three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
3. Identify Action — For each, spot the one simple action it recommends.
4. Compare Action — Compare which action remains robust across versions.
rituals.win: ✓ Three premises produced three worlds; only the robust action survived all of them.
rituals.supports:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FORECAST WITH A LANDING ZONE
rituals.goal: Accuracy can include an honest margin of error.
rituals.steps:
1. Predict Range — Predict a range rather than a perfect point.
2. State Acceptable — State the acceptable error band and why it is reasonable.
3. Measure Reality — After the result, measure reality check: inside, near, or outside the band.
4. Widen the Landing — Adjust future range width instead of declaring success or failure.
rituals.win: ✓ The forecast became a range, so reality had somewhere honest to land.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WAIT FOR THE EVIDENCE THAT CAN EXIST
rituals.goal: Some decisions are early because their key fact has not been born.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Future — Name the future information that could really change the choice, when it becomes available, and how each possible result would alter action.
2. Wait Evidence — Wait only for that evidence.
3. Reject Delay — Everything else is delay wearing a research badge.
rituals.win: ✓ I stopped researching a fact that does not exist yet.

rituals.title: KEEP THE THREAT, ADD THE PERIPHERY
rituals.goal: Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.
rituals.steps:
1. Hold Trigger — Hold the trigger at a manageable centre.
2. Look Away — Without looking away, name five simultaneous peripheral details—colour, distance, movement, light, geometry.
3. Let Central — Let central and surrounding information coexist until the scene feels larger than the alarm.
rituals.win: ✓ The threat stayed visible without swallowing the whole scene.

rituals.title: MOVE NOVELTY TO THE RIGHT TEAM
rituals.goal: Do not fight stimulation seeking; recruit it.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Novelty — Spot the novelty source pulling attention away.
2. Add Controlled — Add controlled variety to the desired task instead: change order, tool, location, soundtrack, colour, or challenge.
3. Keep Goal — Keep the goal constant while refreshing the route.

rituals.title: PIN A RETURN ADDRESS
rituals.goal: A distraction should cost one return address, not a full reconstruction.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Object — Name the exact OBJECT currently carrying the task: document, pan, form, email, shelf, or tool.
2. Place — Notice the precise LOCATION inside it: paragraph three, top-left field, second burner, or blue tab.
3. Choose Verb — Choose one NEXT VERB for that location: compare, type, turn, check, send, or place.
4. Reenter — After the interruption, say the three-part address once and act on the verb without rescanning the entire task.
rituals.win: ✓ Autopilot missed its usual handoff.

rituals.title: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
rituals.goal: Inner agreement is optional; a move that betrays no red line is enough.
rituals.steps:
1. Seat Feelings — Label up to three active emotions as players at the table. Leave them unnamed for the moment; observe first.
2. Vetoes — Give each emotion one veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
3. Clear Board — Cross out actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty. Put it into simple words a child could understand.
4. Choose Survivor — Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it.
rituals.win: ✓ No feeling agreed, but no red line had to be betrayed.

rituals.title: ADD THE TEMPORARY CLAUSE

rituals.title: PRACTISE THE QUALITY ANONYMOUSLY

rituals.title: POWER THEN, RESOURCES NOW

rituals.title: MAKE PROGRESS LEAVE FOOTPRINTS

rituals.title: POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY

rituals.title: LET THE SHAKE BE SMALL

rituals.title: THREE TEMPERATURE FACTS

rituals.title: SCENT THE RETURN

rituals.title: THREE RINGS OF AGENCY

rituals.title: MOVE THE VALUE TO A NEW VESSEL

rituals.title: OPEN THREE ENDING ROOMS
rituals.goal: The future should not be rehearsed as a single locked corridor.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Critical — Spot the critical decision point in the dominant future scene.
2. Create Endings — Create three endings by changing the choice there: cautious, courageous, and collaborative.
3. Cost — Notice the cost and value of each.
4. Keep Best — Keep the ending that best fits evidence and values.
rituals.win: ✓ The compass still works even when the landscape hurts.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Best”; keep the compass.
• Loop back? Use “Cost”.
• “Cost” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Keep Best”: what changed from “Identify Critical”?
• I can use “Create Endings” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Critical → Create Endings → Cost → Keep Best
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not imagine unsafe endings merely to increase variety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: COMMON IS NOT THE SAME AS RIGHT
rituals.goal: Frequency cannot settle an ethical question.
rituals.steps:
1. State Social — State the social norm and your chosen criteria—harm, fairness, consent, dignity, responsibility.
2. Evaluate — Check the norm against each criterion without citing popularity.
3. Keep Modify — Keep, modify, or reject it based on the ethical comparison.
rituals.win: ✓ Popularity lost the argument the moment ethics entered the room.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Modify”; drop the scoreboard.
• Loop back? Use “Evaluate”.
• “Evaluate” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Before/after: “State Social” → “Keep Modify”.
• I can use “Evaluate” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: State Social → Evaluate → Keep Modify
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Consult affected communities and expertise when personal criteria are incomplete.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RETURN THE SHAME TO ITS OLD ADDRESS
rituals.goal: A judging context can end while its standard keeps living inside you.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Whose — Spot whose rule the shame is enforcing and the setting where it was learned.
2. Ask Whether — Check whether you still endorse that standard.
3. Keep Repair — Keep any ethical repair that is truly yours; return contempt, prejudice, or impossible expectation to its source.
rituals.win: ✓ The repair stayed mine. The inherited shame went home.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Repair”; release extra blame.
• Re-entry move: “Ask Whether”.
• “Ask Whether” keeps blame in proportion.
• “Identify Whose” → “Keep Repair”: what changed?
• I can use “Ask Whether” without owning everything.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Whose → Ask Whether → Keep Repair
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek support when shame is severe, trauma-linked, or tied to self-harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
